Hors d'Oeuvres
Les Delices d'Emmenthal- A croquette of Emmenthal cheese made with Bechamel sauce and served with tomato sauce. Bechamel sauce is supposedly named for the Marquis Louis de Bechamel,- a financier rather than a cook. The chances are the real inventor was one of the cooks of Louis XIV.
Paillette aux Anchois- A puff pastry with anchovies. the puff pastry was allegedly discovered by Feuillet, who was the chief pastry cook to the house of Conde.
Croissants au Jambon- A crescent pastry with ham. The croissant dates from the year 1686 when it was first created in Budapest. In that year, the Turks were besieging the city. In order to reach the center of the city, they had to dig underground passages. The bakers who worked during the night heard them and gave alarm. The assailants were repulsed. In order to reward the bakers, they were granted the privilege of making a special pastry in the form of the emblem which decorates the Ottoman flag.
Viand Sechee de Grisons- Air dried cold beef.
Le Caviar Beluga- Fresh caiar has a relatively large, resilient, pleasant appearing eggs. All caviar is salted, but the fresh is not salted so strongly. Eggs are firmer and each one is separated from its neighbour.
Le Ramequin de Fromage- A cheese tart prepared in the Swiss manner.
A barley cream soup from the Canton of Grisons. Barley is one of the most ancient cultivated cereals, and still exists today in its original form on the shores of the Red and Caspian Seas.
La Truite Neuchateloise, Pommes Vapeur- A filet of trout prepared with a white cream sauce. Trout is a species of fish of the same group as salmon, whose flesh, very delicate, is white, pink, or salmon coloured according to the waters they inhabit.
Selle de Veau, Bouquetiere de Legumes- A saddle of veal consisting of the entire back of the animal. It is served with a bouquet of fresh vegetables. The best veal comes from animals aged from two and a half months to three months, fed exclusively on milk, with some eggs towards the end; it must be white with a slight greenish tinge( reddish colouration shows that the animal has been given solid food.)
Sorbet Piper-Heidsieck- is a champagne sherbert. Ices are usually served between the main courses and take the place of the liqueurs, which formerly were served in the middle of the meal.
Perdreau Roti, Sauce Cumberland; Pommes Roesti- a roasted partridge with a jellied sauce of red currant, orange and lemon. The partridge was introduced into France in the fifteenth century by Rene, King of Naples.
Emmenthaler- This is the world favourite that we usually call "Swiss Cheese". The genuine Emmanthaler wheels with the red trademark "Switzerland" stamped on them weigh up to 200 lbs, have a diameter of 30" and are 10" high. The rind is dry and hard. Fine Emmenthaler has a delicious walnut or hazlenut  flavour.
Gruyere- is made in the Swiss-French Cantons; weighs about 100 lbs, has a stronger, more piquant flavour and smaller holes than the Emmenthaler. The rind runs from brown to yellow in colour, and is slightly moist.
Spalen- is a hard cheese amde from whole milk and stands well for many years. It is also known as Habelkase (Plane cheese) because it is often served with a wooden carpenter's plane.
Raclette- is a rather hard cheese made form whole cow's milk. It is made in the mountains of Valais, and is usually consumed a short time after it is made. The name also is used for a method of serving, i.e., scraping the softening block of cheese before a fire and eating it as once.
Souffle Grand Marnier, Les Petit Fours- is is generally recognized that the Arabs and Chinese knew the art of making iced sweets, especially water ices. It was the Chinese who taught the art of ice cream making to the Indians, the Persians and the Arabs. Ice cream and water ices were introduced into France about the year 1660 by a Sicilian named Francisco Procopio. Under the Second Empire, the first coupes, mousses and parfaits were made. The name Petits Four, according to Careme, comes from the fact that they are baked  in a slow oven after the big cakes have been baked, and the temperature of the oven has gone down considerably.
The Wines by Gordon Bass-  In Switzerland, many times more wine is consumed than is made and comparatively little is exported.  Although wine is made in 20 of the 22 cantons, only four areas have commercial significance. Neuchatal, the best known to us, comes from primarily the northern shore of Lake Neuchahtal. The wines of the Vaud originate in the lovely necklace of towns that string along the northern shore of Lake Geneva (Leman), from Geneva through Lausanne, and Monteux to Aigle.  The Valais is the cradle o f the Rhone, and produces some very good  white wine, and the best of the red. The Ticino region, not far from Milan, bears more than a passing resemblance to the wines of Italy.
Dezaley- 1964 - Grossenbacher (Day-za-lay)- The steeply terraced vineyards of Dezaley lie to the east of Lausanne on the north shores of Lake  Leman. Here is produced one of the better dry white wines of Switzerland. Made form the Chasselas grape, it develops quickly, and should be consumed young, fresh and chilled. It is an agreeable light wine for light meals.
Pommery Brut 1961 - En Methusalems- Pommery is one of the great champagne names of the world, and this vintage is one of their finest. The spectacular Methusalem is quite rare in this country and contains eight bottles. Brut champagne(which Pommery is credited with developing) is the driest type made, and all producers use their best wines in the cuvee.
Chateau d'Auvernier, Chateau Bottled Neuchatel (Shah-toe Doh-vern-yerr)- One of the best known of the very good white wines produced in Switzerland. The vineyards lie on the northern shore of Lake Neuchatel, and benefit from the reflected sunshine from the lake, as well as the direct rays of the afternoon sun. It is dry, sprightly, and flowery. A very gracious, pleasant wine with any light meal.
Dole De Sion- Grossenbacher (Dole duh See-ohn)-The best red wine of Switzerland is produced in the lovely Valais. The vineyards lie along the upper Rhone River, and climb to incredible heights on the northern slopes of the valley. Sion is the home of one of the best viticultural schools in Europe. The wine is full boded with good colour and high in alcohol. Both the Pinot Noir grape of Burgundy ad Gamay of Beaujolais are used in this area and the wine resembles those of lower Burgundy and upper Rhone.
Chateau Petrus 1959- Chateau Bottled (Shah-toe Peh-trews)-  Chateau Petrus modestly calls itself "Grand Vin", but is universally regarded as the outstanding wine of Pomerol, and brings prices at least on par with the great first growth clarets of Medoc. There are only eight chateaux in all Bordeaux in this category- 4 in Medoc, 1 in graves, 2 in St. Emilion, and Chateau Petrus in Pomer0l. It is rich and velvety with a lovely colour and splendid balance, this vintage is outstanding, and while today it will still continue and thrive years to come, until it reaches its soft, gracious perfection.
Moet & Chandon- White Seal Extra Dry (Moe-eh Shan-dohn)-  This is an excellent wine for all occasions. A blend of the finest reserves of several years, it appeals especially to popular taste. Moet & Chandon is one of the largest as well as one of the best champagne houses.

Ham, Red Bean and Kaiserdom Smoked Beer Soup with Red Beet- A hearty knife and fork soup with fresh ham and Kaiserdom  smoked beer are cooked all together and served with a dollop of sieved beets. This unique beer is made by smoking the hops.
Cold Soup- Yellow Tomato Caprice Soup with Peccorino (the best salad  soup), served with Proscuitto on Garlic Bread- fresh local tomatoes are a main food item this time of year. This soup is one of the best ways to enjoy tomatoes in their own juices and mozzarella cheese. Yellow tomatoes are low in acid.
Squid Satay in Tortilla Cup on Lobster Curry Soup with Cauliflower- Diced pieces of squid are stewed in an Asian Satay Sauce, then filled into a tortilla cup. The soup is a light curry made with cauliflower and lobster. This soup is served in a plate designed by Jurg Lanzgren- a local artisan living in High Falls.
:::: Supplement for 2 (in place of soup)::::
Stir Fried Lo Mein Noodles in Bangkok Pork Sauce with Chinese Black and White Mushrooms, served w/Mushroom Soy- Chinese white fungus does not resemble a mushroom as we know them. It looks more like coral or sponge and is very light. Sauteed in olive oil with pork pieces, salted black beans, bean curd, scallions and dried day lillies.
Second Course
Pasta
Cheese Ravioli's on Broccoli Rabe Sauce- Mrs Novi's pure semolina pasta is made into a ravioli using the finest of bakers ricotta. The broccoli rabe is made with a little cream, peccorino cheese and pine nuts.
Appetizer
"Zakuska": Catskill Foie Gras and Hijiki Terrine with Mustard Byrd and Chili Garlic "Quinoa", served with a shot glass of Russian Pertsovka Pepper Vodka
Zakuska is Russian for "Hors D'Oeuvres". Foie gras is a product of a small farm in Catskills Sullivan area of New York State. The livers are marinated overnight in Stones Ginger Wine. The Terrine is made by pressing the livers into a mold packed with pureed chicken breast and cream cheese.The Hijiki (pressed seaweed) which we consider its taste and mostly texture to a truffle. Served with a timbal of Quinoa, which is an ancient South American grain staple used by the Aztec Indians.  We blend it with chili and garlic. Mustard Byrd is a combination of mustard from France, Germany and China.
"Zakuska" of Fish: Sole and Maryland Crab, "Mock Strawberry" served with Depuy House Chopped Salad and Red Pepper Mousse, also accompanied by a shot glass of Russian Lemon Vodka- White sole filet is pressed and then wrapped around Maryland Crab mea. It is formed to resemble a strawberry first, then dipped into red pepper puree and sprinkled with sesame seeds. It's baked and served hot with our famous house mined vegetable salad.
Portobello Mushroom and Le Seurre Baby Peas with Cremini Mushroom Cutlet in Eggplant and Cremini Mushroom Sauce ( for people who love mushrooms)- Portobello mushroom is sauteed with peas and served in a sauce made with Cremini Mushroom and pureed eggplant. The Portobello Mushroom was first tasted in Torino, Italy by Chef John Novi. It is as tasty as filet mignon. We hope you enjoy it as John did!
Intermezzo
Entrees
American Striped Bass and Chicken Breast Dim Sum Style on Cognac and Cilantro Sauce accompanied by Pumpkin, and Green Asparagus Tips- Striped Bass is prepared as a mousse with cream and eggs. The Mousse is spread on top of a chicken breast and then wrapped in rice paper before poached in sake and olive oil. This is our introduction to a Fall menu.
Red Snapper Fillet on Salsify Sauce with Cellophane Noodles and Green Asparagus- The Fish is prepared to order- poached or baked. We poach salsify in milk, pureeing until smooth and adding a little reduced cream before service. Saslify is a root plant which dates back to Jefferson's Garden. We are preparing to market this sauce in jars and would appreciate your comments. This entree can be prepared "Spa" no cream Cuisine.
Lamb 3 Ways: Lamb Loin Rare, Smoked Leg of Lamb, and Lamb Skirt Ballantine, served with Sweet Potato in Vietnamese Rice Paper on Papaya Glaze-  A lamb loin is sauteed to order (preferably rare) and served on a sauce made with fresh papaya, which is  blended with Dr. Frank's New York Gewurztraminer. The leg of lamb is smoked on our back porch using mesquite wood. The skirt of ballantine is wrapped around chopped lamb and pistachio nuts.
Beef Tenderloin and Potato Stuffed Onion Skin with Red Beet on Espanole Oyster Sauce- The beef is prepared to order. Mashed potatoes are stuffed into an onion skin and baked. The sauce is a rich veal brown sauce made with tomato and Chinese oyster sauce.
Sweetbread Saute  OR
Fallow Venison Medallion, a la Minute, served with Creamed Spinach, Wild Rice and Kasha, on Brouilly Sauce with Candied Cranberries- Two medallions are sliced from the ultimate of "fresh and tender" venison. They are sauteed at the last minute. The brouilly sauce ( original recipe from Thomas Jefferson's cookbook) is made with a rich demiglace blended with oyster sauce, port wine and currant jelly. Venison surcharge: $10.00
Tour d'Argent of Paris: Fresh Water Prawn Rampant, Baby White Fish, with Timbal of Transylvanian Macadamia Nuts, Sea Scallops, Two Gunkan Rolls of American Sturgeon and Salmon Caviars, served on Wasabi Sauce Rouille- The fresh water prawn is from an American based farm and is split and baked in a hot rouille sauce. One prawn is served along side the baked white fish. It is served under a timbal made with sea scallops and alongside two Chinese rice rolls filled with two caviars. Rouille is similar to a hot Hollandaise. The sauce is made with wasabi powder and cream.
The vegetarian entree is ravioli or a variety of vegetables from our menu.
